requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale: The reviewed tests in `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs` adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`. All three tests are marked with {test} references to it or to its sibling requirement. I did not read the implementation or the `fixture` and `render` helpers. I judged adequacy from the test inputs and assertions. **Obligations and the tests that cover them** - **Show each `habeas:coverage` citation on the file root or an explicit function or method.** - `notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs` builds a fixture with a file-root citation, a free function (`fn[ordinary]`), an impl method (`impl[Worker]/fn[work]`), and an inline-form citation on `fn[unexplained]`. - It asserts that entries exist for all four. - The same test also puts a citation on a nested module and a `child` function inside it. It asserts that this citation does not create an entry and that the text "Nested module must" and the child's docs do not appear. - `citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations` covers the negative cases. A citation on a module, and citation text inside a string literal, produce no entries. The view says "No coverage explanations are present" and contains no "exception proposal" text. - **Each entry identifies its source item and source location.** - The first test checks, for each of the four entries, the heading `## {label}`. - It also checks the exact `Source: code.rs:{first}–{last}` range and "First source citation at line {n}." - **Show fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments that supply the tracked justification.** - The first test shows root docs and root fenced commentary, function docs and fenced commentary, and method block-doc and fenced commentary. It also checks HTML escaping of ``. - `justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments` is table-driven with three cases. Doc-only and fenced-only each show their text under their own heading ("Rust doc comments" or "Citation commentary") with no "No tracked justification" message. An ordinary non-doc comment alone is not shown and yields "No tracked justification is present." - The first test also checks that a child's docs stay with the child. - **Say so when no tracked justification is present.** `fn[unexplained]` shows exactly one "No tracked justification is present." The ordinary-comment case in the table test shows it as well. - **Labels.** - "File-threshold exception proposal" appears exactly once, on the file root. - "Function exception proposal" appears exactly three times, for the function, the method, and the unexplained function. - The nested-module citation is not mislabelled as a file exception. **Gaps considered and not found** - Both citation forms (inline and fenced) are exercised. - Both doc forms (`///` and `/** */`, plus `//!` on the root) are exercised. - Behaviour for multiple citations on one item and for trait-method declarations is not stated by the requirement, so I did not treat it as a gap. - The `{cite}` references to the anchor requirement, which supplies the labelling vocabulary, are applied in the tests' label assertions. I found no plausible requirement-violating behaviour that these assertions would accept.

text: :::{req} index.file_map.notes.justifications
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.
File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
:::{req} index.file_map.notes
Each listed first-party Rust file in a combined or per-test file coverage
map MUST provide access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
